summary: VERIFY round, narrow delta. The delta claim is proven rather than assumed: swapping blob 371c5a05 back in for scripts/coverage.py and 90ca5495 for CoverageGateTest.java into a copy of the index and rehashing `git diff --cached` reproduces 69e30fb7 exactly, so those two files are the whole delta and nothing else moved. All three changes are correct. (1) `measured += 1` after the exclusion check: an excluded module is no longer counted, and the summary line can no longer state a success that did not happen. (2) The measured==0 split is sound -- every class-bearing module with a missing, empty or malformed report sets failed and returns 1 before this point, so at measured==0 with skipped non-empty it is provably true that every module with classes was excluded; the message is accurate. Exit 0 is right: `finish` in lib.sh prints nothing on success (verified), so no green ok line appears; and failing on all-excluded would be arbitrary next to 7-of-8-excluded passing, which already exits 0. (3) Deleting the buildSrc filter does not break a real commit -- verified empirically twice on the extracted staged tree: after a full `./gradlew -p buildSrc test`, buildSrc/build/classes/java contains only `test`, never `main`, so has_classes is False and the loop skips buildSrc; running the real check-coverage.sh on the staged tree printed NOT-MEASURED and exited 0 with no buildSrc line. All four claimed mutations re-derived and each killed exactly the named test, on the extracted staged tree, at 14/14 green baseline. One minor finding, latent and fail-closed. No object-store request is introduced or altered anywhere in this diff; the only cost is one Gradle run per invocation of a gate that is still unwired, and nothing scales with records, shards, partitions or indices.

findings.summary: Deleting the buildSrc filter widens the module set into territory the gate's regeneration step cannot reach, and the comment overclaims. coverage.py now says buildSrc is measured 'like any other module', but check-coverage.sh regenerates with `./gradlew test jacocoTestReport` from the ROOT, which never touches buildSrc: buildSrc is an implicit included build and its tasks are not addressable from the root task graph. Verified on the extracted staged tree -- `rm -rf buildSrc/build/test-results` followed by exactly `./gradlew test jacocoTestReport` exits 0 and does NOT recreate the directory. So buildSrc is in the module list like any other module but is NOT regenerated like any other module, which is the one dimension this commit spent the most effort on.
findings.failure_scenario: Harmless today and it fails closed, which is why this is minor: buildSrc/build/classes/java/main never exists (verified after a full `-p buildSrc test`), so the module is skipped. Two things happen later. First, the day anyone adds a Java source under buildSrc/src/main/java the gate fails on every commit with the remedy line 'Run ./gradlew jacocoTestReport' -- a command that cannot produce a buildSrc report no matter how often it is run, because it does not reach buildSrc and because buildSrc/build.gradle.kts applies only `kotlin-dsl`, never the `jacoco` plugin (the conventions plugin that adds it cannot apply to buildSrc itself). Second, and worse, if someone then adds a `jacoco {}` block to buildSrc and runs `./gradlew -p buildSrc test jacocoTestReport` by hand once, the gate reads that report from then on and never regenerates it -- which is precisely the stale-report defect check-coverage.sh's regeneration step exists to kill, silently reintroduced in the only module where the fix does not apply.
findings.suggested_fix: Not blocking and not necessarily this commit's job. Either narrow the comment to what is true -- buildSrc is in the module LIST like any other module, and its report is not regenerated by this gate -- or, if buildSrc is genuinely meant to be measured, make check-coverage.sh add `./gradlew -p buildSrc test jacocoTestReport` alongside the root call and give buildSrc/build.gradle.kts the jacoco plugin, so that the module the gate refuses to skip is a module the gate can actually measure. A backlog entry naming the trap would also close it.

findings.summary: The new NOT-MEASURED branch prints 'baselines/coverage.txt is a ratchet, not a parking space (testing.md rule 7): each entry names what unblocks it' -- but excluded() accepts a bare module name with no reason at all and nothing refuses it.
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced directly: a baselines/coverage.txt containing the single line `format` produces `WARN format line 10.0% branch 10.0% EXCLUDED:` with an empty reason, then the new NOT-MEASURED text asserting that each entry names what unblocks it, and exit 0. The gate prints a property of the baseline file that it does not check, which is the softer version of the failure class this gate exists to refuse. testing.md rule 7 says exclusions are 'named and justified, never blanket'.
findings.suggested_fix: gate-design rung 3: this is a predicate over one file. Refuse a baselines/coverage.txt line whose reason is empty, rather than printing advice about it. Fine as a follow-up task -- the file does not exist in this tree yet, so nothing is unenforced today.
